# Integrating Google Sign-In into MEGA Android App (MVP Specification)

> ## Implementation status (as-built vs. this spec)
>
> This document is the **original MVP planning spec**, kept for reference. The feature was implemented in the `:feature:sign-in-external` module and now differs from the plan below in several ways. See `feature/sign-in-external/CLAUDE.md` for the module's current design.
>
> - **Android API:** Implemented with **AndroidX Credential Manager** (`androidx.credentials`, `androidx.credentials.play`) + Google Identity `googleid` (`GetSignInWithGoogleOption`). The legacy `GoogleSignInClient` / `play-services-auth` shown in this spec's code snippets and tables was **not** used (it is deprecated).
> - **Backend approach:** Built as **Option B** — the client completes Google Sign-In, decodes the ID token JWT locally (`GoogleIdTokenMapper`), and reuses the existing MEGA login/signup flow (`LoginUseCase` / `CreateAccountUseCase`). No `/auth/google`, `/auth/link`, or `/auth/unlink` endpoint was added.
> - **`sub` as password:** Implemented as described (Google `sub` → MEGA password). This is tracked as known tech debt in **AND-23824** (a stable public identifier used as a password).
> - **JWT validation:** The ID token is **not** signature-verified on the client by design — Play Services / Credential Manager already validated it; the mapper only decodes and extracts claims.
> - **Link / Unlink Google:** **Not implemented.** The current code supports login and auto-signup only; the linking/unlinking flows in this spec are not built.
> - **Rollout:** Gated behind the `ApiFeatures.GoogleSignIn` feature flag (experiment name `gsign`, default **off**).

## Executive Summary

This report defines a minimal implementation plan to add **Google Sign-In** to the MEGA Android app. In this MVP scope, **Apple Sign-In is deferred** to a separate feature. Key assumptions: MEGA’s current auth is email/password, and after a social signup the app treats the social provider’s `sub` as the user’s password (as provided by the question). We will **minimize backend changes** by leveraging existing MEGA APIs where possible. New user flows include Google-based signup and login, and linking/unlinking Google to existing accounts. We outline required endpoints (new or existing), data mapping (`google_sub`, email, name, avatar), and full security checks (OIDC, PKCE, nonce, token validation, minimal scopes, GDPR/CCPA compliance). Android implementation choices (Google Identity Services vs legacy APIs) are discussed, with code snippets and Gradle samples. UI/UX is minimal (Google button, error states). Rollout and monitoring plans ensure safe deployment. The report concludes with role-based task lists, a timeline (4–6 weeks), tables, and mermaid diagrams. Official Google docs are cited throughout; MEGA-specific details (using `sub` as password) are user-provided assumptions.

## Current System Behavior (Assumptions)

- **Auth Method:** MEGA currently uses username (email) and password authentication. After social sign-in, MEGA uses the provider’s unique ID (`sub`) as the user’s password (per user note).  
- **Account Creation:** On Google signup, MEGA creates a new account with the user’s email and sets the password equal to the Google `sub`. It logs the user in automatically.  
- **Linking:** Users with existing MEGA accounts (email/password) can link their Google account via in-app settings (not yet implemented). Linked Google accounts allow login via Google.  
- **Password Storage:** No change to MEGA’s password storage is needed beyond treating `sub` as a password. It’s critical to keep `sub` secret in the client (see Security).  
- **Recovery:** Advanced recovery (e.g. account migration or old password reset) is out of MVP scope (Phase 2+).

No official MEGA SDK documentation for social login was found, so we use the user’s statement of `sub`\=password. If MEGA has an existing signup/login API, we aim to reuse it as noted below.

## MVP User Flows

1. **Google Sign-Up:** User taps “Sign in with Google” on the login screen. The app initiates Google’s OAuth flow, obtains an ID token, and sends it to MEGA’s backend (via a new or existing endpoint). The backend verifies the ID token (see below) and then creates a new MEGA account using the Google email; it sets the MEGA password to the Google `sub`. The user is then authenticated in the app.  
     
2. **Google Sign-In:** User taps “Sign in with Google”. The app again does Google OAuth, receives an ID token, and sends it to MEGA. The backend validates the token and if a matching user exists (linked or with email=sub), logs the user in. Optionally, if using existing MEGA login, the app could log in with `email`\+`sub` directly. (See Backend Options below.)  
     
3. **Link Google Account:** A logged-in user (via email/pass) can choose “Link Google Account”. The app performs Google OAuth, gets an ID token, and calls a MEGA linking endpoint. Backend validates the token and associates that Google `sub` with the user’s MEGA record.  
     
4. **Unlink Google Account:** A user who has linked Google can “Unlink”. The app calls a MEGA API to remove the Google `sub` from their account. After this, Google sign-in will no longer work for this user.  
     
5. **Logout:** Clears the MEGA session in-app. (No special Google API call is required; just clear MEGA’s tokens.)  
     
6. **Token Refresh (Optional):** If MEGA issues a session token that expires, the app may call a refresh endpoint. This is not unique to social login, but any new tokens from Google flow should generate MEGA session tokens normally.

## Data Mapping

- **google\_sub:** The `sub` claim from Google’s ID token (a unique stable user ID). This will be used as the MEGA account password (per current design). Store it securely only on the backend.  
- **email:** The user’s Google email (from the ID token). Used as MEGA username/email. If the user hides their email (rare for Google), handle it per Google policy (usually Google always provides email if requested).  
- **name:** The user’s display name from Google’s profile (ID token or Google People API). Save to MEGA’s profile.  
- **avatar:** The URL of the user’s Google profile photo (if requested). MEGA may fetch or store this as the user’s avatar. This is optional; at minimum, ensure the account is created.

We request at most the `openid email profile` scopes. This gives us sub, email, name, and avatar. Scope minimization follows privacy best practices. Since MEGA already stores names/passwords, mapping to `name` and `avatar` enriches the profile.

## Backend Endpoints and Token Validation

### Endpoint Options

We aim to minimize custom backend work:

- **Option A: New Auth Endpoint (`/auth/google`)** – A dedicated endpoint that accepts Google ID tokens. The backend verifies the token’s signature/claims using Google libraries, extracts `sub` and email, then internally creates or logs in the MEGA user (setting password=`sub` if new). Returns MEGA session token.  
- **Option B: Reuse Existing Login/Signup API** – Instead of a new endpoint, have the client extract `sub` (after verifying the ID token locally) and call MEGA’s existing login API (e.g. `/login`) with `email` and `password=sub`. This avoids new backend code but exposes risk if the client misuses `sub`. If chosen, also consider client-side token validation for security (as below).  
- **Option C: Mixed** – For signup, use `/signup` with email/sub; for login, use either Google ID or email/sub.

For the MVP, we should use **Option B: Reuse the existing login/signup flow**. Since MEGA is an E2EE app, we should avoid sending Google `sub` to the backend through a new Google auth endpoint. Instead, Android can complete Google Sign-In locally, extract `email` and `sub` from the Google ID token, and then reuse the existing MEGA account login/signup API.

Proposed MVP flow:

Android

* Start Google Sign-In  
* Receive Google ID token / JWT  
* Decode JWT payload locally  
* Extract email \+ sub  
* Use existing MEGA API / SDK login flow:  
  * email \= Google email  
  * password \= Google sub

Then Android decides the next step based on the MEGA API / SDK result:

1. Login success  
   * Continue into the app  
2. Account does not exist  
   * Continue with signup using email \+ sub  
3. Account exists but password is wrong  
   * Do not auto-signup  
   * Show: “This email is already registered. Please sign in with your password first.”  
4. Other errors  
   * Show a generic retry message

For Option B (reuse login): after Google returns ID token, the client could decode it (or call tokeninfo) to get `sub`, then POST `{email, password: sub}` to MEGA’s current login. This requires trusting the client not to spoof. Ideally, the app should still verify `id_token` before sending `sub` to backend. If SDK call (like `GoogleSignInClient`) provides an account, the `idToken` is already verified by Google Play services. However, a malicious client could skip it, hence server-side validation (Option A) is safer.

### Data Handling

- Create or lookup user by email. If creating, generate MEGA password=`sub` (or a one-way hash, depending on MEGA’s password policy).  
- For login, match the `sub` with stored password (if MEGA used plain `sub` or its hash). Alternatively, log in the user and then set a session.  
- Ensure linked Google accounts cannot be hijacked: e.g. do not allow linking if that Google `sub` is already linked to another user.

### Security Controls

- **PKCE & Nonce (OAuth Flow)**: On Android, use the OAuth code flow with PKCE for Google (this is handled if using Identity Services) to protect the exchange.  
- **Scope Minimization**: Request only `openid email profile`.  
- **GDPR/CCPA**: Inform users in privacy policy that Google authentication will access their Google profile info (email, name). Only store needed data. Provide account deletion as usual.  
- **One-Time Use**: If using any one-time login links (not needed here), ensure they expire.

## Android Implementation Choices

- **Google Sign-In API**: Use the recommended **Google Identity Services** (also called Credential Manager) approach. The old `GoogleSignInOptions` (Play Services Auth) is deprecated. In practice, `GoogleSignIn.getClient()` with the latest libraries works fine. Alternatively, Google’s One Tap API could be used, but for simplicity we use the standard Sign-In button flow.  
- **Required Libraries**: Add to Gradle:  
    
  implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-auth:21.3.0'  
    
  (or latest version).  
    
- **Configuration**: In the Google API Console, create an Android OAuth client (package name \+ SHA-1) and a separate Web client ID (to use as `requestIdToken`). The Android client ID is used by GoogleSignInClient; the Web client ID is needed on the server to validate tokens (should match `aud`).  
- **Request Code vs Token**: We will use `requestIdToken(serverClientId)` to get an ID token. (A Google OAuth *authorization code* flow could be used but requires server exchange and more backend work; ID token flow is simpler.)  
- **Android Code (Kotlin)**:  
  


| val gso \= GoogleSignInOptions.Builder(GoogleSignInOptions.DEFAULT\_SIGN\_IN) .requestIdToken(GOOGLE\_SERVER\_CLIENT\_ID) // Web client ID for backend .requestEmail() .build()val googleClient \= GoogleSignIn.getClient(this, gso)startActivityForResult(googleClient.signInIntent, RC\_SIGN\_IN)// ...override fun onActivityResult(requestCode:Int, resultCode:Int, data:Intent?) { if (requestCode \== RC\_SIGN\_IN) { val task \= GoogleSignIn.getSignedInAccountFromIntent(data) try { val account \= task.getResult(ApiException::class.java) val idToken \= account.idToken // send to backend or decode } catch (e: ApiException) { // Handle error } }} |
| :---- |


- **One-Tap (Optional)**: Google’s One Tap sign-in (Identity Platform) can simplify UX, but it’s not strictly necessary for MVP. It could be added later to improve adoption.  
- **Apple Placeholder**: Since Apple is out of scope, we include minimal mention or a placeholder (e.g., “(Apple: \[future implementation\])”) and leave Apple column mostly empty in tables, noting it’s deferred.

## UI/UX Requirements

- **Sign-In Button**: On the login screen, add a “Sign in with Google” button. Follow Google’s branding guidelines. Place it above or below existing email/password fields.  
- **Linking UI**: In account settings, show “Link Google Account” (if not linked) or “Unlink Google” (if already linked). These trigger the same Google sign-in flow but on completion call the link/unlink APIs.  
- **Error Messages**: If sign-in fails (invalid token, network error, no Google account available), show a clear toast/snackbar. Example: “Google sign-in failed. Please try again.” If linking fails (e.g. account already linked elsewhere), show an appropriate message.  
- **Consent Screen**: Google will show the user’s account/email selection. No extra screens are needed beyond telling the user which email is used.  
- **Localization**: Use resource strings for any new text.  
- **Loading State**: Indicate progress during network calls.

## Rollout and Monitoring

- **Feature Flag**: Release Google sign-in behind a remote feature flag. Initially disable for all users, then enable for a test group, before full rollout.  
- **Staged Rollout**: Use Google Play’s staged rollout (e.g. 10%, 50%, 100%) to monitor stability.  
- **Metrics**: Log metrics on how many users click Google sign-in, success rates, failures. Backend should log token validation errors.  
- **Monitoring**: Set up alerts for any spikes in errors on `/auth/google`. Use Crashlytics to catch client crashes in OAuth flows.  
- **Rollback**: If issues occur, quickly flip the feature flag or release a fix. Since main change is new endpoints and UI, ensure backend can disable `/auth/google` to prevent new sign-ups if needed.  
- **DevOps Prep**: Coordinate server deploy (new endpoint code, Google client secrets) with app release.

## Tables

**Integration Steps: Google vs Apple (placeholder)**

| Step | Google Sign-In | Apple Sign-In (Deferred) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Dev Account Setup | Google Cloud Console: create OAuth 2.0 client (Android \+ Web IDs) | Apple Developer: create Service ID, enable Sign in with Apple |
| Android SDK | Google Identity Services (play-services-auth) | (None – use web OAuth/AppAuth in future) |
| OAuth Flow on Client | ID Token flow via GoogleSignInClient (requests `requestIdToken`) | (Future: OAuth Code flow in web view or AppAuth) |
| Token Validation | Verify Google ID token on server (iss, aud, exp) | Verify Apple ID token on server (iss, aud, exp) |
| Data Returned | Google `sub`, email, name, avatar | Apple `sub`, email ([relay@appleid.com](mailto:relay@appleid.com)), name (first sign-in only) |
| Backend Endpoint | `POST /auth/google` with `{id_token}` | (Future: `POST /auth/apple` with `{id_token}`) |
| Account Creation/Login | Use `sub` as MEGA password (email from token) | (Future: similarly use `sub` as password) |
| Link/Unlink | `POST /auth/link/google`, `/unlink/google` | (Future: `/auth/link/apple`, `/unlink/apple`) |
| UI Button/Icon | Google button (as per guidelines) | Apple button (for future iOS/Android) |
| Scope/Consent | `openid email profile` | `email name` (future) |

**Backend Endpoints (MVP)**

| Endpoint | Method | Request Body | Response | Server Validation Steps |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **POST** `/auth/google` | POST | `{ "id_token": "..." }` | `{ "session_token": "...", "user_id": "..." }` | Validate Google ID token signature and claims (aud, iss, exp); extract `sub`, `email`, etc.; create or login MEGA user with password=`sub`; return session. |
| **POST** `/auth/link/google` | POST | `{ "user_id": "...", "id_token": "..." }` | `{ "success": true }` | Validate ID token as above; ensure `sub` not already linked; attach `google_sub` to this user. |
| **POST** `/auth/unlink/google` | POST | `{ "user_id": "..." }` | `{ "success": true }` | Authenticated user; remove `google_sub`. |
| **POST** `/auth/refresh` | POST | `{ "refresh_token": "..." }` | `{ "session_token": "..." }` | (If using refresh tokens) validate and issue new session. |
| **(Optional) POST** `/login` | POST | `{ "email": "...", "password": "..." }` | `{ "session_token": "..."}`  | If reusing existing login: accepts `password = google_sub`. Must ensure client-provided `sub` is genuine (recommend verifying ID token). |

## Security Trade-Offs (Backend-Minimizing Options)

- **Using Existing Login (Option B)**: If we skip a new `/auth/google` endpoint and instead let the client do: Google OAuth → get `sub` → call MEGA’s login API (`email`, `sub`), the backend does not validate the ID token. *Trade-off*: A malicious client could forge a `sub` and login as any user. **Mitigation**: Have the client locally verify the ID token (if using Play Services, the returned account is already verified). Still, we **strongly recommend** server-side verification for any production use.  
- **Direct Password Login**: Similar to above, letting the app call `/signup` with `password=sub` works but has same risks.  
- **Mitigation**: If using these shortcuts, one could optionally call Google’s tokeninfo endpoint (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo?id_token=...`) from the backend to verify tokens without a library. This still requires extra backend logic, though possibly simpler than a full library.

## Code Examples

**Server-Side Google Token Verification (pseudocode)**

| \<?phprequire\_once 'vendor/autoload.php';use Google\\Client as GoogleClient;const GOOGLE\_SERVER\_CLIENT\_ID \= 'YOUR\_GOOGLE\_SERVER\_CLIENT\_ID';function verifyGoogleToken(string $idToken): array{    $client \= new GoogleClient(\[        'client\_id' \=\> GOOGLE\_SERVER\_CLIENT\_ID,    \]);    $payload \= $client-\>verifyIdToken($idToken);    if (\!$payload) {        throw new Exception('Invalid Google ID token');    }    return \[        'google\_sub' \=\> $payload\['sub'\],        // Google user ID        'email'      \=\> $payload\['email'\] ?? null,        'name'       \=\> $payload\['name'\] ?? null,        'picture'    \=\> $payload\['picture'\] ?? null,    \];} |
| :---- |

## Sources and References

- **Google Identity (Android)** – recommends using Credential Manager/Identity APIs; legacy GoogleSignIn API is deprecated.  
- **OAuth2/OIDC Best Practices** – use Authorization Code Flow with PKCE for mobile apps; verify ID tokens per spec.  
- **Firebase Auth (Apple)** – notes Google’s `openid email profile` gives email and name, and Apple returns private relay email if user hides it. Nonce generation importance is discussed.  
- **MEGA** – Current behavior (`sub` as password) provided by user; no public docs found on this.

All details above are based on official Google documentation and the provided MEGA assumptions. Unspecified aspects (e.g., minimum SDK) are treated as flexible.
